rule: **Ruby**: `Outer.Inner#method` (constants dotted); `Foo.new` → `Foo#<init>`; constants resolve lexically. A class whose ancestry reaches outside the scan — an external superclass or include, a reopened external class (`class ActiveSupport::TestCase`), or a computed superclass expression (`< Devise.parent_controller.constantize`) — names bare calls not defined by any scanned ancestor `Scope#m`, medium. `self.m()` / `this.m()` / a bare call to a member of the enclosing type → `Type#m`. If `m` is defined only on a superclass that is in the scan, the callee is `Superclass#m`. Constructor / initializer call: `Type#<init>`.
source: KNOWN_GAP: bare new in class methods is not Type#<init>; recv::Const receivers are glued into the type ID
notes: Bare `new(id)` inside a class method is `self.new` with self = the class `Store::Item`, i.e. `Store::Item.new` -> `Store.Item#<init>`, constructor (bare call to a member of the enclosing type + `Foo.new` → `Foo#<init>`). `Store::Item.create` / `::Store::Item.load` / `Store::Item.new`: constants are dotted (`Outer.Inner#method`), so the receiver `Store::Item` (or top-level `::Store::Item`) is the type `Store.Item`; `::` never appears in the ID.
